html:
The Yaghan, or Yámana, are an Indigenous people of the islands and channels south of Tierra del Fuego, around the Beagle Channel and Cape Horn, in present Chile and Argentina. They were the southernmost people in the world.

They lived from the sea, paddling bark canoes between islands with a fire kept burning inside, and hunting sea lions, fish, shellfish and birds. Despite the cold they wore little clothing and kept warm with fires and seal grease. In 1830 Captain Robert FitzRoy took four Fuegians to England, among them the Yaghan boy known as Jemmy Button, and brought them back on the voyage of the Beagle in 1833, with Charles Darwin on board. Missionaries settled at Ushuaia in 1869, and disease soon followed. The Yaghan fell from a few thousand to a few dozen. Cristina Calderón, the last native speaker of Yaghan, died in 2022. Their neighbours were the Selk'nam to the north.
sum: The Yaghan, or Yámana, are an Indigenous people of the islands and channels south of Tierra del Fuego, around the Beagle Channel and Cape Horn, in present Chile and Argentina. They were the southernmost people in the world.
